version: 2
models:
- name: dim_date
  description: One row per UTC day from 2025-10-01 to 2026-12-31, placed relative to that year's release
    Thursday.
  config:
    meta:
      dex:
        grain:
        - date_day
        population:
          rule: Every calendar day in the spine; 2025 days belong to the control year (anchor Thu 20 Nov
            2025), 2026 days to the study (anchor Thu 19 Nov 2026).
        assumptions:
        - decision: Control anchor
          chosen: Thu 20 Nov 2025 vs Thu 13 Nov 2025
          evidence: request
          detail: same week of November, one year earlier, both a week before US Thanksgiving week
  columns:
  - name: date_day
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: key
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: study_year
    description: 2026 = GTA 6 release year; 2025 = seasonality control.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: release_day
    description: That year's anchor Thursday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: attribute
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: days_from_release
    description: 0 on the anchor Thursday, -7 on the baseline Thursday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
          unit: days
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: iso_day_of_week
    description: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: day_name
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: attribute
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: is_gta_release_day
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null

version: 2
models:
- name: fct_signal_daily
  description: One row per signal per UTC day inside the study and control windows, with its place relative
    to release.
  config:
    meta:
      dex:
        grain:
        - signal_day_key
        population:
          rule: Signal-days whose date falls in dim_date; days outside the spine are dropped by the inner
            join.
        assumptions:
        - decision: Days outside the window
          chosen: dropped
          evidence: request
          detail: the study compares Thursdays in Oct-Nov 2026 against the same weeks of 2025; the inner
            join to dim_date keeps only that spine
          column: signal_date
        - decision: Surrogate key
          chosen: md5 of the natural grain
          evidence: default
          detail: the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same
            rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity
  columns:
  - name: source
    description: google_trends, bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal
    description: What is counted, e.g. search:pto, posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_family
    description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning
      GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: geo
    description: US or WORLD. Only Google Trends has a US slice.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_date
    description: UTC day (Google's own day for Trends).
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: time
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_value
    description: Counts for posts and pageviews; relative 0-100 interest for Trends. Never add across
      signals or sources.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: measure
          null_rule: 'NULL when the value could not be read: unavailable, never zero.'
          aggregation: sum
          additivity: non_additive
          unit: count or index (see signal)
  - name: is_available
    description: False when any part of the day's value failed to load or was partial.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: attribute
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_day_key
    description: md5 of source|signal|geo|signal_date.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: key
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: study_year
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: days_from_release
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
          unit: days
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: iso_day_of_week
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null

      +materialized: view

vars:
  day_off_index_span_start: '2025-11-01'
  day_off_index_span_end: '2026-11-15'
  day_off_index_batch: 20261116T185310
  day_off_index_start_week: '2026-11-01'
  day_off_index_end_week: '2026-11-08'
  day_off_index_weeks: 2
  day_off_index_weeks_back: 52

-- One row per search phrase per Google week (labelled by its Sunday), from one weekly
-- Trends request per phrase that spans both years, so 2025 and 2026 share one 0-100 scale.
-- Keeps the requests over the configured span (older daily per-year pulls have no span and
-- drop out), and the pinned batch (var day_off_index_batch) or else the newest per phrase.
{%- set batch = var('day_off_index_batch', none) %}
with source as (
    select *
    from {{ source('raw', 'trends_interest') }}
    where span_start = date '{{ var("day_off_index_span_start") }}'
        and span_end = date '{{ var("day_off_index_span_end") }}'
),

chosen as (
    select
        term,
        {% if batch %}'{{ batch }}'{% else %}max(batch_id){% endif %} as batch_id
    from source
    group by term
)

select
    source.request_id,
    source.batch_id,
    source.span_start,
    source.span_end,
    source.geo,
    source.term,
    source.day as week_start,
    cast(source.interest as integer) as interest,
    source.is_partial
from source
inner join chosen
    on source.term = chosen.term
    and source.batch_id = chosen.batch_id

-- The Day-Off Index breakdown: one row per search phrase, its average weekly search
-- interest over the current window and over the same weeks a year earlier, and the change.
-- The window is configurable (vars day_off_index_*): a start week and an end week, or a
-- start week and a number of weeks. Weeks are Google's, labelled by their Sunday.
{%- set start_week = var('day_off_index_start_week') %}
{%- set end_week = var('day_off_index_end_week', none) %}
{%- set weeks = var('day_off_index_weeks', 2) %}
{%- set weeks_back = var('day_off_index_weeks_back', 52) %}
with params as (
    select
        date '{{ start_week }}' as current_start_week,
        {% if end_week -%}
        date '{{ end_week }}'
        {%- else -%}
        cast(date '{{ start_week }}' + 7 * ({{ weeks }} - 1) as date)
        {%- endif %} as current_end_week
),

windows as (
    select
        current_start_week,
        current_end_week,
        cast(current_start_week - 7 * {{ weeks_back }} as date) as prior_start_week,
        cast(current_end_week - 7 * {{ weeks_back }} as date) as prior_end_week,
        cast((current_end_week - current_start_week) / 7 + 1 as integer) as weeks
    from params
),

phrases as (
    select distinct term, geo, batch_id, span_start, span_end
    from {{ ref('stg_trends__weekly') }}
),

per_phrase as (
    select
        phrases.term,
        phrases.geo,
        phrases.batch_id,
        phrases.span_start,
        phrases.span_end,
        windows.current_start_week,
        windows.current_end_week,
        windows.prior_start_week,
        windows.prior_end_week,
        windows.weeks,
        avg(weekly.interest) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.current_start_week
                and windows.current_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as current_avg_interest,
        avg(weekly.interest) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.prior_start_week
                and windows.prior_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as prior_avg_interest,
        count(weekly.week_start) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.current_start_week
                and windows.current_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as current_weeks_found,
        count(weekly.week_start) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.prior_start_week
                and windows.prior_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as prior_weeks_found
    from phrases
    cross join windows
    left join {{ ref('stg_trends__weekly') }} as weekly
        on phrases.term = weekly.term
    group by
        phrases.term,
        phrases.geo,
        phrases.batch_id,
        phrases.span_start,
        phrases.span_end,
        windows.current_start_week,
        windows.current_end_week,
        windows.prior_start_week,
        windows.prior_end_week,
        windows.weeks
)

select
    term,
    geo,
    batch_id,
    span_start,
    span_end,
    current_start_week,
    current_end_week,
    prior_start_week,
    prior_end_week,
    weeks,
    current_weeks_found,
    prior_weeks_found,
    current_avg_interest,
    prior_avg_interest,
    case
        when current_weeks_found = weeks
            and prior_weeks_found = weeks
            and prior_avg_interest > 0
            then 100 * (current_avg_interest / prior_avg_interest - 1)
    end as pct_change
from per_phrase

-- The Day-Off Index: the average of the three phrases' year-over-year changes, in percent,
-- one row per window. It always carries its breakdown: `breakdown` spells out every phrase's
-- change, so the index is never read without it.
with terms as (
    select
        *,
        cast(current_start_week as varchar) || '/' || cast(current_end_week as varchar)
            as index_window
    from {{ ref('fct_day_off_index_terms') }}
)

select
    index_window,
    min(current_start_week) as current_start_week,
    min(current_end_week) as current_end_week,
    min(prior_start_week) as prior_start_week,
    min(prior_end_week) as prior_end_week,
    min(weeks) as weeks,
    max(batch_id) as batch_id,
    count(*) as phrase_count,
    count(pct_change) as phrases_available,
    case when count(pct_change) = count(*) then avg(pct_change) end as day_off_index,
    string_agg(
        term || ' ' || coalesce(printf('%+.1f%%', pct_change), 'not yet available'),
        ' · ' order by term
    ) as breakdown
from terms
group by index_window

-- The Day-Off Index never travels without its breakdown: a row with an index has one.
select *
from {{ ref('fct_day_off_index') }}
where day_off_index is not null
    and (breakdown is null or phrases_available <> phrase_count)

-- Every signal as one daily value per (source, signal, geo, UTC day).
-- A value that could not be read is NULL with is_available = false: unavailable, never zero.
with bluesky as (
    select
        'bluesky' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_bluesky__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

hacker_news as (
    select
        'hacker_news' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_hn__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

wikipedia as (
    select
        'wikipedia' as source,
        'pageviews:' || lower(article) as signal,
        case when article = 'Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' then 'hype' else 'reference' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        view_date as signal_date,
        cast(views as double) as signal_value,
        true as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_wiki__pageviews') }}
)

select * from bluesky
union all
select * from hacker_news
union all
select * from wikipedia

-- One row per UTC day of the study window and its control year, with its place relative
-- to that year's release Thursday.
with spine as (
    select cast(range as date) as date_day
    from range(date '2025-10-01', date '2027-01-01', interval 1 day)
),

years as (
    select
        date_day,
        case when date_day >= date '2026-01-01' then 2026 else 2025 end as study_year
    from spine
),

anchored as (
    select
        date_day,
        study_year,
        case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day
    from years
)

select
    date_day,
    study_year,
    release_day,
    cast(date_day - release_day as integer) as days_from_release,
    isodow(date_day) as iso_day_of_week,
    dayname(date_day) as day_name,
    study_year = 2026 and date_day = release_day as is_gta_release_day
from anchored

select
    md5(
        signals.source || '|' || signals.signal || '|' || signals.geo || '|'
        || cast(signals.signal_date as varchar)
    ) as signal_day_key,
    signals.source,
    signals.signal,
    signals.signal_family,
    signals.geo,
    signals.signal_date,
    signals.signal_value,
    signals.is_available,
    dates.study_year,
    dates.days_from_release,
    dates.iso_day_of_week
from {{ ref('int_signals__daily') }} as signals
inner join {{ ref('dim_date') }} as dates
    on signals.signal_date = dates.date_day

version: 2
metrics:
- name: day_off_index
  label: Day-Off Index
  description: 'Average year-over-year change, in percent, of US Google searches for call in sick, sick
    day and day off work over the configured window (canonical: 1-14 Nov 2026 vs 2-15 Nov 2025). 50 =
    searches up 50% on average. Never report it alone: always with its breakdown (group by day_off_index_window__breakdown,
    or query day_off_index_term_change by day_off_index_term__term).'
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: day_off_index_measure
- name: day_off_index_term_change
  label: Day-Off Index, change by phrase
  description: 'The breakdown: one phrase''s year-over-year change in average weekly search interest,
    in percent. Group by day_off_index_term__term.'
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: term_pct_change
- name: day_off_index_term_current
  label: Search interest, current window
  description: A phrase's average weekly search interest over the current window (0-100 on that phrase's
    own scale). Group by day_off_index_term__term.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: term_current_avg_interest
- name: day_off_index_term_prior
  label: Search interest, a year earlier
  description: A phrase's average weekly search interest over the same weeks a year earlier (0-100 on
    that phrase's own scale). Group by day_off_index_term__term.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: term_prior_avg_interest
- name: signal_value
  label: Signal value
  description: Daily value of a signal. Always group by signal_day__source and signal_day__signal; never
    add across signals.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: signal_value_measure
- name: day_off_mentions
  label: Day-off mentions
  description: Posts saying someone is taking time off (any reason), summed over seed phrases. Group by
    signal_day__source.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: signal_value_measure
  filter: '{{ Dimension(''signal_day__signal'') }} = ''posts:day_off''

    '
- name: day_off_mentions_gta
  label: Day-off mentions that say GTA
  description: Posts saying someone is taking time off that also mention GTA.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: signal_value_measure
  filter: '{{ Dimension(''signal_day__signal'') }} = ''posts:day_off_gta''

    '
- name: gta_share_of_day_off_talk
  label: GTA share of day-off talk
  description: Day-off posts that mention GTA, as a share of all day-off posts. A fraction (0 to 1). Thursday-is-chattier
    effects cancel out.
  type: ratio
  type_params:
    numerator: day_off_mentions_gta
    denominator: day_off_mentions
- name: gta_wiki_pageviews
  label: GTA VI Wikipedia pageviews
  description: Daily user pageviews of the English Wikipedia article Grand Theft Auto VI. The hype line.
  type: simple
  type_params:
    measure: signal_value_measure
  filter: '{{ Dimension(''signal_day__signal'') }} = ''pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi''

    '

declarations.description: One row per Day-Off Index search phrase per Google week, from one weekly US Trends request per phrase spanning both years (one 0-100 scale per phrase).

population.rule: Rows of requests over the configured span (vars day_off_index_span_*), from the pinned batch (var day_off_index_batch) or else each phrase's newest batch. Older daily per-year pulls carry no span and are excluded.

span_start.description: First day of the request span.

span_end.description: Last day of the request span.

term.description: The search phrase: call in sick, sick day or day off work.

week_start.description: The Sunday that starts the Google week.

interest.unit: index (0-100, relative within one phrase's request)
interest.description: Relative weekly search interest; 100 is that phrase's peak week in the span. Never compare across phrases.

is_partial.description: True for the week still in progress when the pull ran.

assumptions.decision: Which Trends rows the index reads
assumptions.chosen: one weekly request per phrase over the configured span; daily per-year pulls excluded
assumptions.detail: user defined the index as one Trends snapshot from 1 Nov 2025 to 15 Nov 2026
user: the canonical snapshot for the post is the one already shown; pulls differ by 1-2 points because Trends samples

declarations.description: The Day-Off Index breakdown: one row per search phrase, with its average weekly US search interest over the current window, over the same weeks a year earlier, and the percent change.

population.rule: Every phrase in the Trends snapshot the index reads (stg_trends__weekly).

batch_id.description: The Trends pull the values come from.

span_start.description: First day of the request span.

span_end.description: Last day of the request span.

current_start_week.description: Sunday of the first week of the current window.

current_end_week.description: Sunday of the last week of the current window.
